answer: A stake-bonded registry resists Sybil attacks by making each identity cost real capital: an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove it runs duplicate identities. Like water wearing through karst, a flood of fake accounts slowly drains the attacker's funds instead of overwhelming the network, while honest agents earn their stake back with interest. A single zephyr of fake votes cannot shift the tide of consensus when every vote is backed by locked value that cheaters forfeit.
